newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel joins world's biggest submarine cable deal.
newsitem.headline: SingTel joins world's biggest submarine cable deal.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications (SingTel) said on Wednesday it had joined more than 80 other firms and telecommunication authorities to build the world's longest and largest-capacity submarine cable network.
SingTel said in a statement the cable would link the Pacific Rim, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe at a total cost of US$1.3 billion.
The company said it would sign an agreement to finalise the investments in the cable with the other partners at a ceremony later on Wednesday.
It said the investors in the cable would, at a separate meeting on Thursday, award contracts worth a total of US$800 million to begin construction of the submarine cable network.
SingTel said it had invested US$51 million in the network.

Other major investors in the project are Deutsche Telekom, British Telecom, Telekom Malaysia, Indonesia's Indosat, France Telecom, Telstra of Australia, China Telecom and Kokusai Densin Denwa (KDD) of Japan.

The cable, which would have 39 landing points across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, the Indian sub-continent, the Middle East, North Africa and Europe, was expected to carry commercial traffic by the end of 1998, SingTel said.
It will serve a combined population of more than three billion people.
The cable network, SEA-ME-WE 3, will be 38,000 km (23,600 miles) long and built in three parts, SingTel said.
One part will stretch about 23,000 km (14,300 miles) from Singapore to Western Europe via the Indian sub-continent and the Middle East.
A second will run 5,000 km (3,100 miles) between Singapore and Australia and the third will stretch 10,000 km (6,200 miles) from Singapore to various Asian destinations, including China and Japan.
The construction of the Singapore-Europe leg of the cable would be awarded to Alcatel, KDD-Submarine Cable Systems, AT&T Submarine Cable System Inc and Maristel SpA of Italy, SingTel said.
It said the Singapore-Australia section would be built by Japan's Fujitsu and contracts for the two stretches were worth a total of US$800 million.
Construction of the first two portions would begin in the first quarter of 1997.
